steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Active citizenship means taking responsible action to address community or social issues — it goes beyond voting and includes volunteering, campaigning, and community action.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Formal participation: voting, joining a political party, standing for election, contacting elected representatives, attending public meetings.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Informal participation: volunteering, community organising, campaigning, protesting, signing petitions, using social media for civic purposes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The GCSE specification requires students to carry out a citizenship action project — addressing a real issue through research, planning, action, and evaluation.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is active citizenship and why is it important? | Q: Give three examples of active citizenship. | Q: What are the barriers to active citizenship?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Active citizenship means taking part in community and political life to improve society. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Active citizenship is both a topic and a practical requirement — know the theory AND the process Use real examples of citizenship action to illustrate your answers AQA requires you to describe and evaluate your own citizenship action in Paper 2 Section B
